Downgrading a 3x3 conv on the output edge to skip loses capacity (exp 11: -2 to -9), while replacing a conv1x1 is about neutral (exp 9).
Replacing a pooling op with a conv adds learnable capacity (exp 16: +5 to +11), which should beat the effect of replacing other ops.
Replacing the input conv 3x3 with skip removes early feature extraction and hurts on all datasets (exp 7: -5 to -8).
Reconnecting a removed edge with skip adds a useful path (exp 12: +5 to +10), more than swapping one existing op for another.
Restoring a direct input-to-output route via skip helps most when the edge was none (exp 15: +1 to +9).
